parameters.name: key.id
parameters.description: id is a unique identifier provided by the client.

parameters.name: key.category
parameters.description:
category is the category of the log.

 - LOGGING_CATEGORY_UNSPECIFIED: LOGGING_CATEGORY_UNSPECIFIED is an unspecified category. Disallowed for writes.
 - LOGGING_CATEGORY_CHANGECONTROL: LOGGING_CATEGORY_CHANGECONTROL is used for actions executed as part of a change control.
 - LOGGING_CATEGORY_ACTION_EXEC: LOGGING_CATEGORY_ACTION_EXEC is used for actions executed via autofill actions, or the
standalone execution feature.
 - LOGGING_CATEGORY_STUDIO_TEMPLATE: LOGGING_CATEGORY_STUDIO_TEMPLATE is used for studio related executions, e.g. build hooks
or templates being rendered.

parameters.name: key.level
parameters.description:
level is the verbosity level of the log.

 - LOGGING_LEVEL_UNSPECIFIED: LOGGING_LEVEL_UNSPECIFIED is an unspecified level. Disallowed for writes,
but setting this in a GetAll filter returns all logging levels.
 - LOGGING_LEVEL_TRACE: LOGGING_LEVEL_TRACE is equivalent to a trace verbosity log call.
 - LOGGING_LEVEL_DEBUG: LOGGING_LEVEL_DEBUG is equivalent to a debug verbosity log call.
 - LOGGING_LEVEL_INFO: LOGGING_LEVEL_INFO is equivalent to an info verbosity log call.
 - LOGGING_LEVEL_WARNING: LOGGING_LEVEL_WARNING is equivalent to a warning verbosity log call.
 - LOGGING_LEVEL_ERROR: LOGGING_LEVEL_ERROR is equivalent to an error verbosity log call.
 - LOGGING_LEVEL_CRITICAL: LOGGING_LEVEL_CRITICAL is equivalent to a critical verbosity log call.

parameters.description:
LoggingConfig carries the value to set into the datastore.
See the documentation on the LoggingConfig struct for which fields are required.

key.description: key uniquely identifies a standalone log or a series of logs for a single execution.

log.description: log contains the actual log contents.

file.description: file contains the file name of the script being executed, if relevant.

line.description: line contains the line number of the log in the script being executed, if relevant.

audit.description:
audit contains additional audit information added by the service when the log was
written.

tags.description:
tags is a map of tag values that was set on write and can be used in queries
to filter the logs. Some executions will automatically populate some tags. E.g.
change control logs will populate a "changeControlId" and "stageId" tag.

arista.logging.v1.Logging.description:
Logging is used to retrieve non-audit related logs produced by such services as
change controls, studio builds, python autofill actions, etc.

addedBy.description: added_by contains the name of the user who added the log.

arista.logging.v1.LoggingAudit.description:
LoggingAudit contains audit information about the given log. It's added by the logging rAPI
and only accessible in the state model.

arista.logging.v1.LoggingCategory.description:
LoggingCategory describes the possible categories of logging.

 - LOGGING_CATEGORY_UNSPECIFIED: LOGGING_CATEGORY_UNSPECIFIED is an unspecified category. Disallowed for writes.
 - LOGGING_CATEGORY_CHANGECONTROL: LOGGING_CATEGORY_CHANGECONTROL is used for actions executed as part of a change control.
 - LOGGING_CATEGORY_ACTION_EXEC: LOGGING_CATEGORY_ACTION_EXEC is used for actions executed via autofill actions, or the
standalone execution feature.
 - LOGGING_CATEGORY_STUDIO_TEMPLATE: LOGGING_CATEGORY_STUDIO_TEMPLATE is used for studio related executions, e.g. build hooks
or templates being rendered.

LoggingConfig is used to write non-audit related logs produced by such services as
change controls, studio builds, python autofill actions, etc. by providing a key
related to the current execution, the log, and optional metadata such as
file name, line number and tags.

PartialEqFilter provides a way to server-side filter a GetAll/Subscribe.
This requires all provided fields to be equal to the response.

While transparent to users, this field also allows services to optimize internal
subscriptions if filter(s) are sufficiently specific.

TimeRange allows limiting response data to within a specified time window.
If this field is populated, at least one of the two time fields are required.

For GetAll, the fields start and end can be used as follows:

  * end: Returns the state of each LoggingConfig at end.
    * Each LoggingConfig response is fully-specified (all fields set).
  * start: Returns the state of each LoggingConfig at start, followed by updates until now.
    * Each LoggingConfig response at start is fully-specified, but updates may be partial.
  * start and end: Returns the state of each LoggingConfig at start, followed by updates
    until end.
    * Each LoggingConfig response at start is fully-specified, but updates until end may
      be partial.

 - LOGGING_LEVEL_ERROR: LOGGING_LEVEL_ERROR is equivalent to an error verbosity log call.
 - LOGGING_LEVEL_CRITICAL: LOGGING_LEVEL_CRITICAL is equivalent to a critical verbosity log call.

arista.subscriptions.Operation.description:
- INITIAL: INITIAL indicates the associated notification is that of the
current state and a fully-specified Resource is provided.
 - INITIAL_SYNC_COMPLETE: INITIAL_SYNC_COMPLETE indicates all existing-state has been
streamed to the client. This status will be sent in an
otherwise-empty message and no subsequent INITIAL messages
should be expected.
 - UPDATED: UPDATED indicates the associated notification carries
modification to the last-streamed state. This indicates
the contained Resource may be a partial diff, though, it
may contain a fully-specified Resource.
 - DELETED: DETLETED indicates the associated notification carries
a deletion. The Resource's key will always be set in this case,
but no other fields should be expected.
 - PARTIAL_DELETE: PARTIAL_DELETE indicates the associated notification carries
deletions of specific fields within the last-streamed state.
The Resource's key is always set.
 - BATCH_START: BATCH_START indicates the beginning of a batch of notifications.
This message will carry no resource value. A corresponding BATCH_END
message will mark the end of the batch. The semantics of what a
batch means is defined by the service.
 - BATCH_END: BATCH_END indicates the end of a batch of notifications that
began with a BATCH_START message. This message will carry no
resource value.

fmp.DeleteError.description:
DeleteError defines the set of delete error types.

 - DELETE_ERROR_UNSPECIFIED: DELETE_ERROR_UNSPECIFIED indicates that the delete error
is not specified.
 - DELETE_ERROR_UNAUTHORIZED: DELETE_ERROR_UNAUTHORIZED indicates that the user is not authorized
to perform the specified delete.
 - DELETE_ERROR_INTERNAL: DELETE_ERROR_INTERNAL indicates that the server encountered an
unrecoverable error on the specified delete.
 - DELETE_ERROR_UNDELETABLE_KEY: DELETE_ERROR_UNDELETABLE_KEY indicates that the specified error is
not allowed by the service.
